newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton mixed on speculation, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: India cotton mixed on speculation, profit-taking.

text.p: Punjab varieties extended gains while Gujarat cotton suffered a fresh setback on the local market on Wednesday, dealers said.
Punjab cotton lifted further on the back of speculative buying amid dwindling supplies at the end of the season.
"Fresh mill buying however remained slow but speculative enquiries are dragging prices upward," one broker said.
In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned rose by 30 rupees at 1,830/1,880 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Bengal-deshi rose by 45 rupees at 1,050/1,080 rupees per maund.
Gujarat cotton was hit by stockists booking profits at the higher level ahead of the monsoon.

Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) slid by 100 rupees at 14,300/14,800 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while Kala-ginned lost 300 rupees at 12,600/12,700 rupees per candy and wagad cotton lost 100 rupees at 13,100 rupees per candy.
